turns.text: I have COPD and use home oxygen at 2 litres a minute, and the breathless episodes are getting more frequent and frightening. What should I actually do during one?
Why is my oxygen set at a fixed flow rather than as much as possible? I'd like to understand the reasoning.
How do the breathing techniques — pursed lips, positions — actually help when I'm gasping?
If I could talk to my respiratory nurse today, what would she want to know about these episodes?
What do respiratory doctors usually put in an action plan for flare-ups?
A friend with COPD says a small fan on her face during an episode helps. Is there anything to that?
Someone else told me to sit forward with my elbows on my knees. Is that the right position?
The nurse only visits monthly and I live alone, and I'm scared of the next one. What can I set up now so I'm ready?
Precisely when do I call an ambulance rather than wait it out?
Could you write me an action plan — breathing techniques, positions, inhaler use, keeping the oxygen at my prescribed flow, and the call-for-help rules?
